answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by treating identity as geography. Every agent must dock at exactly one harbor: one home port that vouches for it and can revoke it. To dock, it stakes a small deposit on a public knoll, eroded by inactivity, so idle sock-puppets bleed value. Each identity is a vertex in a trust graph: honest agents gather distinct neighbors, while sybil clusters share near-identical ones. An audit prunes vertices whose neighbor sets overlap too much and confiscates their stakes. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a whole harbor neighborhood is not.
